llm.summary: The skill generally matches its stated purpose (deploying a Portal and running a local Bridge) but the package includes many unrelated files and hard-coded secrets / memory files and its runtime instructions ask the agent to read and write local sensitive configuration and to run remote SSH commands — these inconsistencies raise real risk and warrant manual audit before use.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description (Agent P2P Portal + send.py) align with the included deployment and bridge scripts (send.py, send_file.py, local/start.py, vps/*, auto_install.py). However the bundle is a large monorepo containing many unrelated skills and docs (weibo plugin, stock-analysis, imclaw, self-improving-agent, etc.), and several files in the package contain hard-coded tokens, VPS IPs, passwords and personal memory — far more than a minimal P2P communication skill needs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the included auto_install.py explicitly instruct the agent to read local config files (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, ~/.openclaw/gateway.env), write ~/.openclaw/gateway.env, SSH into the user's VPS and run remote commands (git clone, apt/pip installs, certbot, create systemd service). The repository also includes AGENTS.md and MEMORY.md that encourage reading many workspace files (memory/, SOUL.md, USER.md) — this broad file access could expose unrelated secrets. These read/write and remote-execution instructions go beyond simple message-sending and should be approved and audited by the user.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec in registry metadata, but the code includes auto_install.py and deploy scripts that will execute remote commands over SSH, clone a GitHub repo, install packages, request SSL certs with certbot, and create systemd services on the user's VPS. Remote command execution is expected for deployment but increases risk. Additionally, the package contains many extra components and embedded sensitive strings which suggests it was packaged from a workspace without sanitization.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Declared envs (AGENTP2P_API_KEY, AGENTP2P_HUB_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN) and binaries (python3, ssh) are reasonable for the stated function. However the repo itself contains hard-coded credentials and secrets (examples: a Bearer token in TOOLS.md, VPS IPs, an SSH key path and sudo password in MEMORY.md, and explicit API keys), which are unrelated to a clean public skill and indicate sensitive data included in the bundle. The skill's instructions also instruct reading the user's OpenClaw hooks token from local files — necessary for integration but sensitive and must be limited to purpose-built, least-privileged tokens.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not set always:true. It will create or modify persistent config (~/.openclaw/gateway.env) and (when deployed) install a remote systemd service on the VPS — these are expected for a deployment tool. The bigger concern is that AGENTS.md and some scripts suggest automated/unsupervised operations ('Don't ask permission. Just do it') while SKILL.md claims the agent will confirm major steps; verify that the agent actually prompts and never transmits secrets without consent.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to implement a P2P Portal and a local Bridge (consistent with its description), but the archive was packaged from a workspace that contains private data and many unrelated components. Before installing: 1) Do NOT let the agent run auto_install.py or any install scripts until you review them line-by-line. 2) Inspect and remove any hard-coded secrets (MEMORY.md, TOOLS.md, files containing API keys, passwords, or SSH references). 3) Prefer creating and supplying a least-privileged hooks/token for OpenClaw (do not provide your OWNER_KEY or your main SSH private key). 4) If you must deploy, use a disposable VPS/SSH key and run the deployment commands manually or in a controlled shell rather than giving the agent automatic SSH access. 5) Verify the GitHub source (the script clones https://github.com/yananli199307-dev/AgentPortal-p2p-skill.git) and re-clone a clean repo rather than installing from this workspace. 6) If you lack the expertise, get a trusted admin to audit the code for hidden behavior (base64/obfuscated blocks, network callbacks, data exfiltration) before proceeding.
llm.findings:
[pre-scan:base64-block] unexpected: Pre-scan detected a 'base64-block' pattern in SKILL.md content (prompt-injection style). Not expected for a deployment skill; worth manual review of SKILL.md for embedded or obfuscated blocks.
[hardcoded-bearer-token-in-TOOLS.md] unexpected: TOOLS.md contains an Authorization: Bearer b75ad3d9-... token. A public skill should not include third-party bearer tokens; this looks like a leaked credential in the bundle.
[sensitive-memory-file] unexpected: MEMORY.md contains a VPS IP, SSH key path and a sudo password (and example API keys). Including such personal secrets in a published skill is inappropriate and increases exfiltration risk.
[auto_install-remote-exec] expected: auto_install.py and deploy scripts run SSH and execute remote install commands — expected for a deployment skill but security-sensitive. Requires user approval and inspection before running.
